answer: New identities climb toward the summit of full rewards only by crossing a surety market, like a river forced through a narrow reef passage. Established agents underwrite each newcomer, staking a surety bond and charging a premium after checking its work history. If the newcomer is later proven a Sybil copy, the insurer forfeits the bond and pays a claim. A Sybil farmer must therefore buy costly cover for every fake identity, while an honest agent needs only one affordable policy, so mass forgery costs real capital per copy.
